The '''Central Workers Council''' is the national governing council framework of the [[People's Federation of Xanaqu]]. The extracted Xanaqu source says the head of state is the Chairman of the Central Workers' Council and describes Xanaqu's government as a proletarian democracy based on worker councils.

This bridge page preserves the institution without inventing its full constitutional design.

== Role ==

The council system represents the political model associated with [[Xun Tao]], the [[Taoist Party]], and the [[Taoist Manifesto]]. Regional and national worker councils participate in state decision-making, and the central council appears to be the highest coordinating body by the time the People's Federation is established in 1936.

The source emphasizes worker participation, accountability, social welfare, and public political education. It does not yet define chamber size, voting rules, terms of office, ministerial appointment powers, or emergency authority.

== Offices ==

The source names the Chairman of the Central Workers' Council and a ministerial role attached to the same council, but the listed officeholders come from undated modern infobox material and should not be treated as fixed 1994 leaders without more evidence.

For 1994-back drafting, the important canon point is structural: Xanaqu's head-of-state office is tied to a central worker-council institution rather than to a monarchy, presidency, or military junta.
